_policy: Objects that hardware reads or writes on its own, so that a volatile qualifier on them is evidence, not steering, wherever tools/volatile_rom_proof.py shows the qualifier's effect on their accesses. A dma-source or dma-target entry names a RAM object (a data symbol, its mapped address and its size) and ROM code that programs a DMA channel with it: the code's bytes are pinned by SHA-256 and the transfer is read off the instructions at every run. A scanline-payload-getter entry names a function whose pinned code returns a scanline task's payload, read off its instructions and its two callees' at every run, with the scanline pipeline that hands the payload to the HBlank DMA bank. A scanline-callback-allocator entry names the function that makes its r0 a new scanline task's callback, pinned by SHA-256, with the same pipeline, whose manager calls that callback with the task's payload and the bank it submits for HBlank DMA. A reviewed-ram entry is different: it names an ordinary RAM object that no hardware is shown to touch, admitted case by case under a user ruling for the functions it lists only, with the review's ROM evidence. The proof re-reads that evidence at every run: the function's bytes, pinned by SHA-256, and each listed reload, which must be a load of the object that the non-volatile build drops, merges or moves, after an earlier access of it. What the review could not prove is printed in each report as its premise. The default stays hardware-only. Listing an object admits nothing by itself. ONLY the repository maintainer may add an entry; agents park the function and cite the evidence instead.
